correctness.rationale: Fix n,w,p and use h=sqrt(1-r). Conditional on independent Gaussian innovations, a monotone threshold equation has a unique solution. Weighted first-order noise cancels after recentering, yielding the second-order threshold with the derivative ratio equal to q+2phi(q)/p. Gaussian-maxima truncation at h^(-1/2) bounds Taylor remainder expectations by O(h^3) and the complement by exp(-c/h). The exact moments Em=0, Em²=sum w_i² and Ev=1-sum w_i² produce the coefficient. Mills strict inequality q+phi(q)/p>0 proves strict sign. Numerical quadrature of 12 bivariate cases corroborates but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2024 research explicitly asks whether harmonic-mean merging is subuniform for positive Gaussian dependence and only provides selected simulations. This analytic result establishes local positive inflation for every fixed significance level and all finite dimensions/weights and gives its exact dependence on level and weight concentration. The information identifies the leading calibration failure relative to comonotonicity, a natural dependence boundary, without claiming the entire conjecture.
